record.paper_title: Some open problems related to small divisors
record.context_brief: Non-perturbative periodic solutions for Hamiltonian PDEs
record.original_question: Find a non-perturbative method for constructing time-periodic solutions of a Hamiltonian PDE, excluding traveling-wave solutions.

evidence.quote: Problem 4.3.2 (S. Kuksin) Find a non-perturbative way to obtain time­ periodic solutions of an Hamiltonian PDE (the solutions should not be trav­ elling waves).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Develop a non-perturbative method for constructing time-periodic solutions of a Hamiltonian partial differential equation. More precisely, consider a Hamiltonian PDE of the form
   u_t = J ∇H(u),
where u(t,x) belongs to a suitable function space over a spatial domain (e.g. the torus T^d or an interval with appropriate boundary conditions), J is a symplectic structure, and H is a Hamiltonian functional. Produce a method—not relying on a small-parameter (perturbative) expansion around an integrable or linear equation, and not relying on KAM/Nash–Moser-type perturbation theory near such an unperturbed system—that establishes the existence of genuine time-periodic solutions u(t+T,x) = u(t,x) for some period T > 0. The required solutions must not be traveling waves; that is, they should not be obtainable from a stationary profile via the ansatz u(t,x) = v(x - ct) for some constant velocity c.
artifact.status_search_result: The literature on Hamiltonian PDEs continues to construct time-periodic and quasi-periodic solutions predominantly via perturbative techniques (KAM theory, Nash–Moser/Lyapunov–Schmidt reduction, and Birkhoff normal forms), all of which rely on smallness assumptions or proximity to an integrable/linear regime. No general non-perturbative construction (excluding traveling waves) appears to be available, and the problem is still cited as a guiding open question in surveys on Hamiltonian PDEs.

status_evidence.title: Hamiltonian PDEs (Handbook chapter) — S. B. Kuksin
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of methods (KAM, Nash–Moser) for periodic and quasi-periodic solutions of Hamiltonian PDEs, all perturbative in nature.
status_evidence.claim: Available constructions of time-periodic solutions to Hamiltonian PDEs are perturbative; no non-perturbative method is presented.

status_evidence.title: Weakly non-linear completely resonant Hamiltonian PDEs — S. Kuksin (Fields slides)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses constructions of time-periodic solutions via perturbative/normal form techniques near resonant linear equations.
status_evidence.claim: Standard approaches remain perturbative; the non-perturbative question is left open.
